compiled_state.description:
## Problem

AGENTS.md carries two pieces of guidance that read as contradictory when an agent is about to
run a gate:

- **"Bound every background process you spawn"** says to bound helpers AT SPAWN in wall-clock
  time (`timeout 120 …`), because an unbounded busy loop reparents to PID 1 and runs for days.
- **"Gate duration expectations"** says `review-plan` takes 15-20 minutes and a
  completion-verifier close 9-11 minutes.

An agent that reads the first rule and then backgrounds a `review-plan` will put a `timeout` on
it. That is the wrong move and it is expensive: the gate is a billable multi-call LLM run, so
truncating it wastes the whole call, produces no verdict, and — worse — the truncation is easy
to misread as a gate failure rather than a bound the agent imposed on itself.

I nearly did exactly this in the session that filed this ticket, and the operator corrected it:
"Don't bound the background helper at spawn. 15-20 minutes is a guideline, not a hard limit."

## Why the two rules do not actually conflict

The bounding rule targets an **unbounded** workload — `while True: pass`, `yes > /dev/null` —
which has no reason to stop and no natural end. A gate run is a **bounded** workload that
simply takes a long time: it terminates on its own with a verdict. The section already says
"Prefer a bounded workload to an unbounded one. A loop that counts to a fixed bound and exits
cannot leak; only an infinite one can." A gate is that bounded workload. The guidance is right;
it just never says so where an agent about to run a gate will look.

## Fix

State the carve-out in the bounding section itself, and make the duration line say that the
figures are guidelines rather than ceilings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The bounding section explicitly excludes long-running gate/LLM operations from the
      at-spawn `timeout` rule, and says why (bounded workload, terminates on its own).
- [ ] The duration line states the figures are guidelines, not limits, and that a gate may
      legitimately exceed them.
- [ ] The carve-out names the concrete failure it prevents: a truncated gate wastes a billable
      run and reads as a gate failure.

## Verification

    grep -n "gate" AGENTS.md   # the carve-out appears in the bounding section

file_impact.reason: Carve gate/LLM runs out of the at-spawn wall-clock bounding rule and mark the gate-duration figures as guidelines, so an agent does not put a timeout on a review-plan and truncate a billable run

compiled_state.title: AGENTS.md: the at-spawn bounding rule reads as applying to gate runs, which would truncate them
